dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked/1: Middle of %2$s, and %3$s has %4$s. I've been standing there looking at it since first light.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked/2: I've got %4$s in %3$s, and it being %2$s doesn't help. No good answer yet.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked/3: Bad news out of %3$s: %4$s. And %2$s is not the season to be finding it.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked.res: Let me give you a hand with it.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked.acc: Two of us can shift %2$s before dark. All right. That's better than the plan I had.
If you'll take a corner of %2$s, I'll take the other. Yes. Let's do that.
Then we move %2$s today. I'd been telling myself it was a one-man job.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.blocked.exp: It came on with %2$s, and I was slow to see it. That's the honest version.
You get %2$s and then you get everything that follows from it. That's where I am.
I'd say the whole of it is %2$s. Everything else is me arguing with the weather.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.recovered/1: Good news about %2$s. It's come back. Loud as anything this morning.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.recovered/2: I'd written off %2$s. Went out yesterday and there they were, working.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.recovered/3: It turns out %2$s is right again. Took the whole spring, mind.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.recovered.e: Dry boards and time, mostly. I moved %2$s off the ground and stopped fussing at it.
I stopped opening %2$s every other day. Turns out they wanted leaving alone.
New comb and a warm week. That, and I put %2$s where the wind doesn't get at it.
dialogue.bees.scene.wet_hive.recovered.t: Kind of you. I'll admit I'd stopped expecting it.
Thank you. It's a small thing to be pleased about and I'm pleased about it.
I'll take that. Not much goes right on a schedule out here.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead/1: Coming into %2$s I'll want a second stand built. That's the whole of my planning so far.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead/2: There's a fair bit to do before %2$s is out. Frames first, then the far end of the row.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead/3: I've been thinking about %2$s more than today, if I'm honest. Wax to render, stands to shift.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead.r: I can spare a day when you start.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead.e: Frames first. They want scraping while the weather still lets me work outside.
Build the stand, render the wax, then leave them be. In that order, if nothing interferes.
Nothing clever. A stand, a fence to keep the stock off it, and patience.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.season_ahead.a: I'll hold you to that. Bring gloves and don't wear anything dark.
A second pair of hands would halve it. Come by early, before they're up.
That's an offer I'll take. Most people say it and then remember something else.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.evergreen/1: They're fine. Busy. Bees mostly get on with it whether I'm watching or not.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.evergreen/2: Nothing to report, which in this trade is the good kind of nothing.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.evergreen/3: Quiet week. I stood at the row for a while and then went and did something useful.
dialogue.bees.scene.hives.evergreen.answ: Two strong stands and one I'm not sure about. That's the usual arithmetic.
They take the clover down the lane before anything else. Creatures of habit.
Loudest around noon. If you want to see them working, come at the middle of the day.
dialogue.bees.followup.wished/1: Thank you. I'll say the same to whatever you're carrying.
dialogue.bees.followup.wished/2: Appreciated. Come by and see whether it worked.
dialogue.bees.followup.wished/3: That's decent of you. I'll take all the luck going.
dialogue.bees.leaving/2: Mind the row on your way past.
dialogue.bees.plain.respond: The bees are the bees. Some years they're kind about it.
mcaconversations.slot.bees_the_split_ske: the skep I split in spring
